title: QBR - Archimedes AI - Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage growth, cost drivers, P95 latency regressions in April, options for Dedicated capacity, upcoming feature roadmap (batching/quantization suggestions), and agreed next steps: run a dedicated pilot for customer-critical endpoints and share updated pricing/benchmarks and SOC2 docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, with Omar and Jin. We'll do a quick QBR, 45 minutes. Laura / Archimedes team, can you confirm attendees?
[00:07] Laura: Yep Laura here, Ravi, Katrina, Tom — thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Speaker 1: Cool, we'll jump in. Agenda is usage, costs, reliability, roadmap.
[01:05] Omar: Quick folk to note, thanks for the usage spikes last quarter, saw a 2.3x increase in inference volume, mostly customer-facing summarization and recommendations.
[01:20] Ravi: Yeah we're seeing that, also higher token counts per request — longer contexts — which bumped costs, and a couple of P95 latency blips in April.
[01:35] Jin: Right, on the P95 we correlated to a small fraction of requests that had KV cache misses during prefix-heavy sessions; the runtime had to rebuild some caches while autoscale was hitting new nodes. Noted that your traffic pattern included bursts around releases.
[02:02] Laura: Could you explain KV cache miss — we sometimes see K V cash in notes — sorry — what does that mean for us?
[02:10] Jin: Sure, so Redwood runtime uses prefix / KV caching to avoid recomputing context for common prompts. When the cache misses, those requests do a bit more work and can bump latency. With Dedicated capacity or pinned capacity you reduce that churn because your working set stays warm.
[02:35] Maya: High level — there are three levers for the cost/latency tradeoff: batching policies, caching config, and quantization/model selection. We'll propose quick changes after today.
[03:00] Katrina: From product standpoint our main success criteria are sub-300ms P95 for recommendations and under $0.40 per 1k tokens cost net — open to tradeoffs but that's our target.
[03:18] Maya: Noted. Current P95 for the recommendation endpoint is ~380ms during peak and unit cost is about $0.62 per 1k tokens when using current hosted model v2-small-opt.
[03:32] Tom: Is that including the embedding pre-query step? Sometimes we do an embedding + generation pipeline.
[03:39] Omar: Good callout — embedding step is separate, that added roughly 40ms on average; the numbers earlier were generation only. End-to-end for your pipeline is closer to 420ms P95.
[04:05] Ravi: The cost jump was around when we expanded to EU region, any cross-region fallbacks that could add cost?
[04:12] Jin: There is smart routing; when EU capacity was constrained we routed some requests to US-hosted instances which increased tail latency and inter-region egress. We can pin region or use Dedicated in EU to avoid that.
[04:31] Laura: Security question — for Dedicated or Private, how does KMS tie in? We need customer-managed keys.
[04:38] Maya: We support KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated with envelope encryption and audit logs in the Console. We'll share the SOC2 + architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[05:02] Speaker 2: A few callouts on SLA — you asked about percent of requests covered: Dedicated gives the highest throughput and SLA, hosted is best for quick velocity.
[05:20] Katrina: We're leaning to Dedicated for the recommendation endpoint, but want sandbox/shared for dev. Rough timeline: pilot in next 6 weeks and production by Q3 if pilot looks good.
[05:35] Maya: That timeline works. We'll scope a Dedicated pilot: reserved pool, canary rollout for 4 endpoints, load target of 600 qps combined, and a baseline cost estimate.
[06:00] Tom: On instrumentation — we need token-level cost breakdown per route in Console and tracing hooks into our APM.
[06:12] Omar: Console already exposes per-route token and latency breakdowns; we can export traces to your Datadog/Splunk. Jin will help set up the tracing hook.
[06:45] Laura: On quality regressions — we had a couple prompts that changed after model updates, any eval tooling?
[06:52] Maya: Redwood Optimize has a prompt/eval harness and regression alerts tied to your golden prompt set. We can onboard your regression set to alert on drift.
[07:05] Ravi: Cost optimization options? We tried quantization but saw slightly worse generation quality.
[07:12] Jin: Quantization profiles come in different flavors — int8/4 mixed precision, some models are more quant-friendly. We can run side-by-side A/B on your prompts to measure quality delta and token latency/cost improvements.
[07:40] Speaker 1: We ran a quick sim last month and saw ~30% cost reduction on heavy batch workloads with little user-visible quality drop for non-critical prompts.
[08:05] Katrina: For critical endpoints we prefer no quality regression even for 5% cost.
[08:10] Maya: Understood — we'll propose a hybrid: Dedicated pinned for critical endpoints (no quant) and shared/quantized for lower priority routes.
[08:30] Tom: Anything on autoscaling — in April we hit an incident where autoscale lagged and caused timeouts.
[08:38] Jin: That was a combination of burst traffic and the autoscaler cooldown; we'll suggest tuning policy: faster scale-up thresholds, pre-warmed burst capacity, and a fallback to a compatible cheaper model to avoid timeouts.
[09:05] Laura: If we move to Dedicated, what's the minimum commit?
[09:10] Maya: Typical committed pool starts at 8 GPUs for the class you run; we'll send concrete numbers. Pricing is monthly reserved with burst credits.
[09:25] Ravi: We also care about data residency and audit logs for compliance.
[09:30] Omar: Private deployment can be VPC-hosted; logs and audit trails can be exported to your SIEM, and we support SAML SSO and RBAC. We'll provide the Private deployment checklist.
[10:00] Speaker 3: Quick health metrics review — usage: 2.3x last quarter, errors: steady 0.8% overall, P95 spike in Apr to 620ms on peak day, since stabilized to 410ms after the infra patch.
[10:25] Laura: That 0.8% errors — what's most common?
[10:30] Jin: Mostly transient timeouts and a handful of malformed requests from a client-side change.
[11:00] Tom: Can you share the detailed logs for the April spike? We raised a ticket but haven't dug in.
[11:08] Omar: We'll attach the April incident timeline and logs to the follow up and include suggested mitigations.
[11:30] Laura: On roadmap, any upcoming features that would help us?
[11:36] Maya: Coming features: improved continuous batching to reduce tail cost, KV cache persistence across restarts, and a per-route A/B rollout system. All slated for Q3 / early Q4.
[11:55] Ravi: KV cache persistence sounds huge. Will that reduce cold-start P95?
[12:00] Jin: Yes, persisting working sets reduces rebuilds; we'd expect up to 20-30% P95 improvement on cache-sensitive workloads.
[12:22] Katrina: What's the estimated lift to try a Dedicated pilot? We need an internal approval packet.
[12:28] Maya: We'll prepare a one-pager: cost model, SLOs, pilot scope, and success criteria (P95 <300ms, no >1% errors, cost per 1k tokens < $0.50 effective after committed discounts).
[12:45] Tom: Also need a checklist: integration work, expected downtime, migration plan.
[12:51] Omar: We'll include migration steps: canary traffic, dual-write period, rollback plan.
[13:10] Laura: Any security concerns with Private vs Dedicated?
[13:15] Jin: Private gives the strongest controls (customer VPC, customer-managed KMS, air-gap option). Dedicated hosted still provides encryption at rest and in transit plus audit logs, but keys are RW-managed unless you opt for Private.
[13:35] Katrina: Ok — decision tree: pilot Dedicated in EU for rec endpoint, dev on hosted sandbox, evaluate quantized routing for low-priority endpoints.
[13:45] Maya: We'll also run a benchmark for your top 10 prompt families to compare v2-small-opt vs. v2-medium-quant and a CPU fallback cost estimate.
[14:05] Tom: Timeline recap? Pilot kickoff in ~6 weeks, a 4-week pilot, review and decision end of Q3.
[14:12] Maya: Yes. Follow-ups: pricing breakdown, SOC2 & security pack, April incident logs, Dedicated pilot proposal, and benchmark results.
[14:30] Speaker 2: Quick questions from Laura in chat about tag-based billing per-team?
[14:35] Omar: Console supports tag-based billing export; we'll demo and send sample exported CSV.
[15:00] Laura: Thanks everyone.
[15:03] Maya: Thank you — we'll send notes and next steps.
[15:05] [end of recording]

Attach April incident timeline and logs
Run benchmark for top 10 prompt families and share results
